# Part VI: Orchestration: Agents, Retrieval, Context {#part-orchestration .unnumbered}

> "reasoning traces help the model induce, track, and update action plans."
>
> Shunyu Yao et al., ["ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)

Once a model can be served, the next step is to give it work that does not fit
inside one answer. It must read, remember, retrieve, call tools, wait for
results, revise its state, and sometimes coordinate with other agents. This part
is about the machinery around the model when the unit of work becomes a task
rather than a completion.

@sec-training-agents begins with the training problem: an acting system is
rewarded for a whole trajectory, a full run of the agent acting step by step,
instead of for a single answer. @sec-agent-architectures and @sec-the-harness
then describe the execution loop and the runtime that turns each of its steps
into bounded, observable work. Between them, @sec-memory-systems separates
logs, workspaces, and long-term stores, and @sec-personalization follows the
memory that outlives any task: the product's memory of its user, and its
effects on markets, privacy, and sycophancy. @sec-computer-use extends
the action space to the screen itself, where the agent operates software built
for human eyes and hands. @sec-multi-agent-systems asks
when more than one model call gives a useful signal rather than duplicated
failure. Outside knowledge has to be found, ranked, embedded, and treated as untrusted
input, and @sec-rag-retrieval and @sec-embeddings explain how. @sec-context-engineering
closes the part by treating the context window as a bounded view that the
system assembles for each model call, with decisions about budget, placement,
compression, and recursion.

Orchestration has few clean primitives. In an agent run, state leaks between
steps, tools hang, memory becomes both evidence and liability, and the boundary
between model behavior and system behavior blurs. For each design, the chapters
ask which loop owns the next decision, what state it can see, and what can stop
it when a step fails or the environment changes.
